Commentary.Commentary: We are back for England's reply. In case you were wondering, 14 overs are remaining in the day's play. Rohit Sharma with some final instructions in the Indian huddle before they spread to take their places in the field. Out walk the two openers of England, Zak Crawley and Ben Duckett, who will look to get their side off to a good start. It will be Jasprit Bumrah to start with the new ball for India. Let's go...
... FOURTH INNINGS ...

That is the end of India's second innings and the hosts stand strong with a big lead of 398 runs. India started with a first-innings lead of 143 runs and after batting 78.3 overs, have managed to put on another 255 runs on the board. Both Yashasvi Jaiswal and Rohit Sharma were dismissed by James Anderson in the first half hour of Day 3 and then it was the Shubman Gill show, who managed a brilliant century, his first at his new position in Test cricket, batting at number 3 for India. Gill scored 104 and was the lone batter who looked in full control. With Axar Patel being the second-highest in the innings with 45 runs, the rest of the Indian batters went back cheap. England were good with the ball and kept picking up wickets. Apart from one good partnership between Axar and Shubman, no other partnership was big enough for India. At Tea, India looked on course to stretch their lead over 400 but they lost their last four wickets for just 27 runs to be bowled out for 255. For England, Tom Hartley was the pick of the bowlers with a four-wicket haul while Rehan Ahmed chipped in with three wickets. It all started with James Anderson's twin strikes whereas the debutant, Shoaib Bashir had one wicket to his name. The visitors will be pleased that they did not allow India to run away with the game and it will be interesting to see how they approach this chase of 399 with two days plus half a session left in the Test.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! The debutant, Shoaib Bashir breaks through for England! First successful review of the series from England and what a time to get it right! Bashir offers flight and bowls it on off, Shubman Gill pulls out the reverse sweep but the ball is not that full to execute that shot. The ball does not turn much and it goes on to hit the gloves and lobs up only as far as the keeper. The England players think it has come off the pad and they appeal for LBW, which is turned down by the umpire. Amidst all this, the keeper, Ben Foakes is alert to the situation and sees the lobbing up. He takes it cleanly and then appeals for caught behind. The umpire is still unmoved and England take the review. There is a clear spike on the UltraEdge and the centurion will have to make the long way back. End of a special knock from a special player and he walks off to a standing ovation from the crowd and his teammates.

Starting the day at a disadvantage, England required a strong first hour to regain control of the game. James Anderson spearheaded their effort with two crucial wickets in the first half-hour, dismissing Rohit Sharma and Yashasvi Jaiswal. Despite Anderson's twin strikes, the spinners struggled to exert pressure from the other end. Just when the partnership between Shreyas Iyer and Shubman Gill were beginning to trouble Ben Stokes, a moment of brilliance from the English skipper helped them see the back of Iyer. Rehan Ahmed backed it up with the wicket of Rajat Patidar to peg India back a bit. That said, Gill is standing strong for India and the hosts have a substantial lead of 273 runs. It will require another strong first hour after Lunch to keep India in check. As for India, Shubman Gill will look to carry on and stretch the lead to make it more difficult for England in the second innings. Join us back at 12.10 pm IST (6.40 am GMT) for what promises to be another riveting session of Test cricket.

SESSION SUMMARY - 102 runs, 30 overs and 4 wickets. End of a pretty entertaining morning session on this 'Moving Day'! The momentum shifted back and forth during the two hours of play, but India have maintained control of the game. India started the day with a lead of 171 runs and the onus was on the Indian openers to set a solid foundation. However, the hosts faced an early setback as Rohit Sharma departed early, adding only a single run to his overnight score. Yashasvi Jaiswal followed suit shortly after, putting India in a spot of bother.  Shubman Gill and Shreyas Iyer then formed a crucial partnership to weather the storm and kept ticking along nicely. Having survived a few close chances early on, Gill made it count and got to his fifty. Iyer and Gill looked largely untroubled until the former was dismissed. The debutant, Rajat Patidar had a short stay at the crease after which Shubman Gill with the newly arrived Axar Patel held fort to take India into Lunch with a lead of 273 runs.
